# 2.7 - Train Your Own AI {.unnumbered}

Until now, someone else trained the AI: the class, or Mr. Ross.

Today, **you** train an AI to recognize hand signs, with your camera, in about 10 minutes. No code. No account.

Then you try to fool it. That is the most important part.

:::{.agenda}
**Today's Plan** (40 minutes)

- [🔥]{.icon} **Warm Up** What should it learn? [4 min]{.time}
- [👥]{.icon} **Learn Together** How Teachable Machine works [6 min]{.time}
- [🛠️]{.icon} **Try It** Train it, then fool it [22 min]{.time}
- [💬]{.icon} **Talk About It** Would it work for everyone? [8 min]{.time}
:::

:::{.objectives}
- [ ] I can train an image AI with my own examples.
- [ ] I can test my AI and find where it fails.
- [ ] I can explain why an AI fails on examples that are different from its training data.
:::

::::{.vocab}
:::{.word-cards}
- [🏷️]{.icon} {{< glink label >}}: the right answer for an example, like "rock"
- [🏋️]{.icon} {{< glink training >}}: showing an AI many examples so it can fix its weights
- [🧪]{.icon} {{< glink "test data" >}}: new examples the AI never trained on
:::

[Printable lesson sheet](/handouts/Unit_2/2.7_Train_Your_Own_AI.pdf){target="_blank"} - the sheet you write on today.

{{< warmup >}}

You can train an AI to tell apart any pictures your camera can see. What would you teach it? Write two ideas on your sheet.

Examples: rock and paper. Thumbs up and thumbs down. A pen and a pencil. Your face and your partner's face.

{{< learn >}}

### 2.7.1 - How Teachable Machine Works

**Teachable Machine** is a free tool from Google. It runs in your web browser.

| Teachable Machine word | What it means | What we called it |
|---|---|---|
| **Class** | one kind of thing, like "rock" | a {{< glink label >}} |
| **Samples** | the pictures you take for a class | training examples |
| **Train Model** | the network fixes its weights | {{< glink training >}} |
| **Preview** | try it on new pictures | {{< glink "test data" >}} |

:::{.gotcha title="Your pictures stay on your computer"}
Teachable Machine trains in your browser. Your pictures stay on your computer unless you choose to save your project to Google Drive. **Do not save it.**

Ask before you take pictures of anyone else.
:::

{{< tryit >}}

### 2.7.2 - Train It

Work in a group of **2 or 3**, with one computer that has a camera.

:::{.steps}
1. Open [Teachable Machine](https://teachablemachine.withgoogle.com/train/image){target="_blank"}. Choose **Standard image model**.
2. Rename **Class 1** to "Rock" and **Class 2** to "Paper."
3. For each class, press **Webcam**. Make the hand sign. **Hold to Record** about **50 pictures**. Move your hand a little while you record.
4. Press **Train Model**. Wait. Do not switch to another tab while it trains.
5. In **Preview**, make each sign. Watch the bars. Is your AI right?
:::

:::{.gotcha title="Class size and cameras"}
**Small class:** each pair trains its own model, then you swap computers and test each other's. **Large class, or no cameras?** Mr. Ross trains one model on the projector. Everyone comes up and adds pictures of **their** hands. A class model has more kinds of hands in it. Is it better?
:::

### 2.7.3 - Fool It

Now try to make your AI wrong. Change **one thing** at a time. Write what happened on your sheet.

- Use your **other hand**.
- Move your hand **very close** to the camera, then far away.
- Turn the **lights off**, or stand in front of a bright window.
- Let your **partner** make the signs.

:::{.think title="Why did some tricks fool your AI?"}
Your AI learned from **your** hand, in **this** room, in **this** light. When something new came in, it had never seen anything like it. So it guessed.

This is true for every AI, even very big ones. **An AI is only as good as its training examples.**
:::

{{< talk >}}

Your AI worked well for **you**. Would it work for everyone? Who was **missing** from your training pictures?

:::{.frames}
- My AI was fooled by ... because ...
- My training pictures were missing ...
- A face AI trained only on people from one country might ...
:::

{{< further >}}

:::{.project title="Day 2: Make It Harder to Fool"}
Open Teachable Machine again with your partner. Train Rock and Paper like yesterday.

1. Press **Add a class** and name it "Scissors." Record about 50 pictures.
2. Try two new tricks. Change the **background**: hold up a book or a poster. Then make the sign with a **glove** or a sock on your hand.
3. Now make your AI harder to fool. Add more **kinds** of examples: both hands, different people, near and far, different light. Train again.
4. Test all the tricks again. Did your AI get better? Write what changed on your sheet.
5. **Class model:** train one model with pictures from **everyone**. Test it on a teacher who was not in the pictures. Is it better than a one-person model?
:::

:::{.project title="Hello in Three Languages"}
Make an **Audio project** in Teachable Machine. Teach it to recognize "hello" in three languages that people in your class speak. Record each word from several people. Does it work for someone new?
:::

:::{.project title="Sort the Recycling"}
Train an image model with three classes: **paper**, **plastic**, and **metal**. Use real objects from the classroom. Test it on objects it has never seen. Where does it make mistakes?
:::
